incidents.victim: Pope's Worldwide Prayer Network ("Click to Pray" app)
incidents.vector: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in a public API endpoint let anyone enumerate user records with no authentication.
incidents.impact: Names and email addresses of 700,000+ users and staff exposed and trivially scrapable; vulnerability remained unpatched as of publication.

incidents.victim: Zimbra Collaboration Suite users (governments, defense, financial sector)
incidents.vector: Zero-click/half-click phishing exploiting a Zimbra webmail zero-day (CVE-2025-66376) to inject JavaScript that harvests credentials and mail data.
incidents.impact: Since July 2025, exfiltrated 90 days of email, credentials, and 2FA codes from government, defense, and financial targets across NATO, Ukraine, and Africa; joint advisory issued by agencies from 15+ countries; unpatched instances still being exploited.

incidents.vector: Attacker wiped the entire land registry database after a failed extortion attempt.
incidents.impact: Halted all property transactions nationwide; notaries unable to authenticate sales or register mortgages.

incidents.vector: Unconfirmed; hacker sent media a sample of allegedly stolen records before the company confirmed a breach.
incidents.impact: Customer account data compromised for a subset of nearly 5 million customers, including partial card/bank numbers, names, addresses, and dates of birth.

incidents.vector: Chained exploitation of CVE-2026-60137 and CVE-2026-63030, begun within three days of public disclosure.
incidents.impact: Widespread attempted remote takeover attempts across one of the largest attack surfaces on the internet.

incidents.vector: Attacker used an autonomous AI agent (Hermes, run in an unrestricted "YOLO mode") to conduct the intrusion.
incidents.impact: Ministry systems compromised; discovered after a researcher found an internet-exposed attacker directory containing malware payloads and intrusion logs.

incidents.vector: Breach of fintech systems; stolen customer data used to fraudulently open rent-to-own agreements.
incidents.impact: Approximately $13 million in fraudulent loan/rental agreements opened on the Acima marketplace using stolen customer data.

incidents.vector: Attackers obtained the cross-chain bridge's private keys to sign fraudulent transactions.
incidents.impact: $24 million in cryptocurrency stolen from the AFX Trade bridge.

incidents.vector: Exploited the same smart contract function abused in a prior May 2026 hack of the same bridge.
incidents.impact: $7.5 million in Ether stolen; second hack of this bridge in 2026 (total ~$19 million across both incidents).

incidents.vector: Exploited a smart contract handling Cardano-Binance cross-chain transactions.
incidents.impact: Nearly $10 million in crypto assets stolen within an eight-minute window before the platform could react.
Sensitive customer data exposed, including the last four digits of payment cards.

incidents.vector: Ransomware attack against a frozen-food logistics and shipping provider.
incidents.impact: Disrupted shipments across ~7,000 refrigerated vehicles and 141 logistics centers; caused shortage warnings at Kentucky Fried Chicken franchises in Japan; personal data confirmed stolen and partially leaked online.

incidents.vector: Compromised credentials for a third-party supplier's file-sharing platform.
incidents.impact: Technical documents belonging to a supplier stolen; Everest group demanded a $12.3 million ransom, which Stadler refused; no impact to Stadler's own systems or trains in service.

incidents.vector: A contractor published 844MB of sensitive CISA data, including AWS GovCloud admin credentials, in a public GitHub repository for roughly six months undetected.
incidents.impact: Exposed AWS GovCloud administrative keys and plaintext credentials for internal systems; no confirmed misuse, but CISA took 48+ hours to rotate keys after external notification despite nine prior automated alerts going unanswered.
